questions.text: On which day is candling performed to check egg hatchability?
questions.explanation: Candling — using light to inspect eggs for fertility — is performed on Day 10. It is a sample check, not all eggs are candled.

questions.text: After how many days in the setter are eggs transferred to the hatcher?
questions.explanation: Eggs are transferred from the setter to the hatcher after 18–18.5 days. The transfer process is automated.

questions.text: What rule applies when eggs are moved from Cold Store to the setter?
options: Random selection based on batch size
Heaviest eggs are always set first
questions.explanation: The FIFO (First In, First Out) rule applies — the oldest batch is always used first when moving eggs from Cold Store to the setter, ensuring egg freshness and traceability.

questions.text: What types of egg rejects occur during the setter-to-hatcher transfer?
options: Grade C, Grade D, Grade E
Rots, Short, Setting Break, Transfer Break
questions.explanation: The diagram identifies four reject types at the setter-to-hatcher transfer: Rots, Short, Setting Break, and Transfer Break.

questions.text: After how many days in the hatcher do chicks hatch out?
questions.explanation: After the hatcher receives the setted eggs, chicks hatch out in 2.5–3 days.

questions.text: What happens to cracked eggs in the Cold Store (Track A)?
options: They are sent to the hatcher
They are moved to the setter
They are rejected at the Cold Store stage
They are candled first, then rejected
questions.explanation: Cracked eggs are noted as rejects at the Cold Store stage: 'Note: Reject — Cracked eggs.' They do not proceed to the setter.

questions.text: What is done to chicks immediately after hatch-out?
options: They are immediately shipped to broiler farms
They are graded, then vaccinated, then graded again
They are weighed and sexed only
They are placed in cold store for 24 hours
questions.explanation: After hatch-out: Grading → Hatch-out vaccination → Grading after vaccine → Grade A chicks received. Rejects (dead, culls, inject-dead, inject-culls) are removed.

questions.text: What are the five reject egg categories listed in quality/by-product handling?
options: Grade B, Grade C, Grade D, Infertile, Overweight
Small, Cracked, Dirty Nest Box, Miss Shell, Offal
Rots, Short, Transfer Break, Setting Break, Empty
questions.explanation: The five egg reject categories listed in the quality/by-product handling section are: Small, Cracked, Dirty Nest Box, Miss Shell, and Offal.
